audit.why: 51.3% over 2920 games with EVEN 5.5/10 is consistent: Lissandra wins every lane exchange against a champion with no dash before 6, but the matchup is decided by whether Destiny gets value elsewhere, not by the duel.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0..3].side and phases[5..6].side read Skill while content win[0..6] read Lissandra on all seven rows — six rows rendering two different answers. packet.levelChart is Lissandra on all seven.
audit.why: Twisted Fate has no dash and no escape until Destiny at 6, must walk to 200 range to land a locked card, and Lissandra's Q outranges his walk-up at 725. Every stage of this lane belongs to her; the Skill rows were stale.
audit.corrected: phases[0..3].side and phases[5..6].side -> Lissandra, with the four early whys rewritten in the same proposal. phases[5].why and phases[6].why already described Lissandra winning.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two factual errors in the content layer: spikes[0].text and mid both call Ice Shard a stun ('then Ice Shard the stun', 'Ice Shard hard-stuns him'). Ice Shard is Lissandra's Q and it slows; the root is Ring of Frost (W). early also claims 'your passive shields don't matter' — Twisted Fate's passive is Loaded Dice, bonus gold on a kill, and there is no shield anywhere in his kit. packet.suspectNames flags 'Wild Card' in spikes[1].text; the ability is Wild Cards. breakdown.cooldowns held no digit.
audit.why: Riot's text: Ice Shard 'deals magic damage and slowing Move Speed'; Ring of Frost 'dealing magic damage and rooting them'. Loaded Dice: 'Upon killing a unit, Twisted Fate rolls his lucky dice receiving 1 to 6 bonus gold.' Pick a Card is a flat 6s at 200 range and is an auto-attack reset; Wild Cards is 6/5.75/5.5/5.25/5; Destiny is 170/140/110 and enables a Gate that 'teleports Twisted Fate to any target location in 1.5 seconds'.
audit.corrected: Q and W given their correct effects, the shield claim removed, Wild Cards spelled correctly, and real cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: missingInteractions flags autoreset-burst-tell: Pick a Card is an auto-attack reset, so the visual tell is the wind-up as he locks the card, not the cast. Nothing on the page said so.
audit.why: The kit file carries autoReset on Pick a Card and his combo opens with that attack, so stepping back on the lock rather than on the attack is what avoids it.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim under 'Self-R the all-in and counter-burst'; dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under 'Tomb him while his burst is already spent'. dontsFull[0].d was a name-swappable template.
audit.why: The bodies did not explain their titles.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten to their titles using Pick a Card's 200 range and 6s cooldown and Wild Cards' 5s at rank 5.

edits.before: Q-shatter the wave and chip his melee step-ups — your early Q harass is better than the lane gives it credit for.
edits.after: Level 1 is yours: Ice Shard reaches 725, his Wild Cards have to thread the wave, and he has no dash to trade back.

edits.before: W online: anyone who closes onto you eats a root. The anti-engage layer is already real at level 2.
edits.after: W online at 450 — he has no dash, so any card he walks up to land puts him inside your root.

edits.before: E claw completes the kit — you now have the lane's strangest engage and a guaranteed exit. Greed carefully; the claw is slow.
edits.after: E completes the kit: a 1050-range claw onto a champion with no mobility at all until Destiny at 6. Keep the recast as your exit.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q spam stops hurting your mana. Chip Twisted Fate every time he touches the wave.
edits.after: Lost Chapter steadies your mana; chip him every time he steps up to land a locked card at 200 range.

edits.before: - Twisted Fate Pick a Card (Gold): matchup-defining — The locked gold card starts every trade and gank — back off the moment it glows yellow. It governs your forward steps. - R Frozen Tomb (self-cast) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Pick a Card is a flat 6s and it is an auto-attack reset, so the wind-up as he locks gold is your cue to step back, not the cast. - Wild Cards is 6s at rank 1 and 5s at rank 5. - Destiny is 170s at rank 1; while it is up, ping every lane. - Your tomb is 120s — keep it for his Gate.

edits.before: Twisted Fate wins by landing Pick a Card (Gold), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Twisted Fate wins by ignoring you, farming safely with Wild Cards, and turning a 170s Destiny into two kills in the side lanes.

edits.before: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive.
edits.after: Q him at 725 as he lines up Wild Cards, and the moment he walks to 200 range to land a card, W-root and rotate — he has no dash to leave.

edits.before: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: Clawing in to poke a farming Twisted Fate — you spend a 24s exit on chip damage, and his gold card stuns you the moment you land.

edits.before: Carry through picks — claw-root-tomb converts vision into kills better than any control mage; the map shrinks every time your E is up.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the roam — when Destiny lights up, claw over the wall and arrive first; a Twisted Fate caught mid-Gate is a free tomb.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt: claw into every river skirmish first, tomb the carry, and snowball picks — Twisted Fate farming under tower can't stop a roaming Lissandra.
edits.after: Ahead, hunt: he has no dash and a 170s ult, so claw onto him every time Destiny is down, tomb him, and take the tower he cannot defend alone.

edits.before: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive.
edits.after: He has to walk to 200 range to land a locked card — self-R through the gold-card stun, surface untargetable, then W-root him and Q him down.

edits.before: That is Twisted Fate’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Wild Cards comes back every 5s at rank 5; you cannot out-wait the poke, only sidestep it.

edits.before: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: A Twisted Fate with his card spent has a 6s wait and no dash — Q and walk him down instead of spending a 120s tomb on him.

edits.before: With Q, W, and E online you can walk Twisted Fate down: Q for the poke and slow, then Ice Shard the stun, and he has no dash to escape your follow-up auto trades.
edits.after: With Q, W, and E online you can walk him down: Ice Shard at 725 for the poke and slow, then Ring of Frost to root at 450 — he has no dash to escape the follow-up.

edits.before: Your R can cancel his channeled Destiny ult or lock him the instant he tries to Gate/roam, and it out-ranges any Wild Card he throws back.
edits.after: Your R stuns him out of the 1.5-second Gate the instant he tries to roam, and it is point-and-click where his Wild Cards can be sidestepped.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are entirely yours. His only proactive tool is picking Gold/Red card, and Ice Shard hard-stuns him out of the channel or the throw. Track his ult timer at 6 and be ready to R-cancel his global roam, then punish the tempo you gain by shoving and diving.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are entirely yours. His only proactive tool is locking a gold or red card and walking to 200 range, and Ring of Frost roots him out of that walk-up. Track his 170-second Destiny at 6 and be ready to stun him out of the 1.5-second Gate, then shove and dive on the tempo you gain.

edits.before: You out-stat Twisted Fate at every early level: your Q is a longer-range, harder-hitting poke and your passive shields don't matter because he can't burst you. He is a farm-and-roam champ with no waveclear edge and no mobility, so freeze or slow-push and force him to farm under threat of your E-Q-W all-in.
edits.after: You out-stat Twisted Fate at every early level: Ice Shard is the longer-ranged, harder-hitting poke and he has no burst to answer it with. He is a farm-and-roam champ with no mobility at all until Destiny, so freeze or slow-push and force him to farm under threat of your E-Q-W all-in.

notes: Six of seven chart rows had the full layer on Skill while the content layer and packet.levelChart both read Lissandra; I moved the full layer onto the content values, so no paired win[N] edit exists to write — the content values are already the targets. phases[5].why and phases[6].why already described Lissandra winning and needed no rewrite. Two hard factual errors fixed in the content layer: Ice Shard was called a stun in two places (it slows; the root is Ring of Frost) and early claimed Twisted Fate has a shielding passive (Loaded Dice is bonus gold). packet.suspectNames was right — 'Wild Card' corrected to 'Wild Cards'. No lint findings on report[] and nothing there names a fabricated ability, so report[] was untouched. I described R as stunning him out of the 1.5-second Gate rather than 'cancelling a channel', since Riot's text gives the 1.5-second teleport but says nothing about channel-interrupt rules.
